## Question (from Shinichi's `ms_SN.docx` comments)

Reviewing the manuscript equations, SN flagged the asymmetry-correction term and asked
(comments #50–#52, #66):

- "some brackets have been omitted?" — the correction argument had no parentheses.
- "logup looks confusing log(up)??" — `\log\!\tfrac{\text{up}-0.5}{...}` renders as *logup*.
- "log is always log10 or loge???" / "log = log10 or loge?" — is the bare `\log` base-10
  or natural?

Daniel's instinct was that all logs should be `log₁₀`. That is **half right**: the answer
is that there are two distinct log families and they are *not* the same base.

## Finding

**1. Time / dose logs are log₁₀ (already correct).** `log₁₀ t`, `log₁₀ t₅₀`,
`log₁₀ t_ref`, `mid`, `log₁₀ 60`, `z·log₁₀(r*/100)` all live on the base-10 exposure-time
axis. These were already written `\log_{10}` and are unchanged.

**2. The asymmetry-correction term is a natural log (ln), not log₁₀.** The term is
$\frac{1}{k}\,\ln\!\left(\frac{\text{up}-p}{p-\text{low}}\right)$. Three independent
confirmations:

- **Model definition.** The 4PL denominator is $1+\exp\!\big(k(\log_{10}t-\text{mid})\big)$
  — base $e$. Solving $p(t)=p^\*$ inverts the `exp`, which yields a **natural** log:
  $$
  p = \text{low} + \frac{\text{up}-\text{low}}{1+\exp(k(\log_{10}t-\text{mid}))}
  \;\Rightarrow\;
  \log_{10}t_{p} = \text{mid} + \tfrac{1}{k}\ln\!\Big(\tfrac{\text{up}-p}{p-\text{low}}\Big).
  $$
- **Code (ground truth for the published numbers).** `R/predict_heat_injury.R` computes
  the correction with R's `log()` — natural log — e.g. line 98
  `log((up - survival_target) / (survival_target - low))` and line 130
  `c_target <- log((up - target_surv) / (target_surv - low)) / k`, then feeds it into
  `exp(k * (log10(dose) + c_target))` (line 132).
- **The supplement's own derivation already says so.** `supplement.qmd` Step 6 is literally
  titled *"take natural logs of both sides"* — but then wrote the ambiguous `\log` symbol
  next to all the `\log_{10}`, which is exactly what confused SN.

So forcing everything to `log₁₀` would have made the equations inconsistent with both the
fitted model and the code. Decision confirmed with Daniel 2026-07-03:
**`\ln` (with parentheses) for the correction term; keep `\log_{10}` for time/dose.**

**3. The `\log z` positivity link is also natural log.** `z` is fit on the log scale
(`priors.R` uses `log(3)`; the formula uses `exp(logz)`), so `\log z_{ij}` → `\ln z_{ij}`.
The base is immaterial to inference here (pure positivity transform); the change is for
notational consistency only.

### Sanity check (SN's own)
When the design anchors low≈0, up≈1: $(\text{up}-0.5)/(0.5-\text{low}) = 0.5/0.5 = 1$ and
$\ln 1 = 0$ — the correction vanishes and `mid(T) ≈ log₁₀ t₅₀(T)`. This is the
strict-equivalence regime.

## Edits made (2026-07-03)

Every bare correction `\log` → `\ln\!\left(\dots\right)`; `\log z` → `\ln z`.

- **`ms/ms.qmd`**: Eq. 4 (L283), Eq. 5 (L289), Eq. 6 / LTₘ (L297), the inline correction in
  the direct-parameterisation paragraph (L308), and `\ln z_{ij}` in the empirical-direct
  model Eq. 11 (L744).
- **`ms/supplement.qmd`**: α definition (L384), the T-varying callout (L859, L862, L865),
  the full step-by-step derivation (L4243, L4248, L4258, L4264, L4282), the LTₓ
  generalisation (L4295), the "correction vanishes" block (L4324, incl. `\ln 1`), and
  `\ln z_{ij}` (L1658).

No numbers change — this is notation only; the code already used natural log.
